problem: The text chain is rectifier then smoother then comparator, but the figure jumps straight from the Rectifier block to the Threshold block. A student copying the diagram for the exam will leave out the smoothing stage, which is exactly what stops the comparator chattering.
fix: Add a block between rectifier and threshold: {'id': 'smooth', 'label': 'Smoother', 'note': 'low-pass / averager'} with edges rect → smooth → thr, matching the six written steps.

problem: The rule 'Too high a threshold gives no reward. Too low a threshold gives reward all the time' assumes the tone itself is the reward. Two paragraphs earlier the EMG design sets the threshold below resting level, so the tone is on at rest and silence is the reward. With silence as reward the rule reverses, and a student can carry the wrong one into the exam.
fix: State the rule for both cases: when the tone is the reward, too high a threshold never rewards and too low a threshold rewards constantly; when silence is the reward (EMG relaxation, threshold below resting level), too low a threshold keeps the tone on and never rewards, too high a threshold keeps silence on all the time.

problem: Units are given for Vin, Vout and T but not for Venv, and 'average' hides that the smoother is a low-pass filter with a time constant. T is said to be 'in the same unit as Venv', which leaves the student guessing.
fix: Write: Venv is the smoothed envelope in µV, obtained as a running average (low-pass filter) of |Vout|; T is the threshold in µV.

problem: The remark that full loop design is taught in only a few syllabi appears three times (lead, Section 3, and again in the closing line of Section 3). Repetition wastes space on a phone screen.
fix: Keep one such sentence, for example in the lead, and delete the rest.
